perspective:
Harold’s accessible information:

- He is a project manager. His project team’s progress is suffering, and he feels frustrated, anxious, and worried. He believes the team is not performing well due to a lack of motivation.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a friend and police officer whom he relies on for advice. He arranged to meet Arthur at a local coffee shop.
- At the coffee shop, Harold told Arthur: his team seems completely unmotivated, it is affecting progress, and he is at his wit’s end.
- Harold heard Arthur say: motivation can be tricky; Harold should try understanding what drives each team member individually; people need to feel valued and understood personally; Harold should try one-on-one conversations.
- Harold told Arthur he had not really done that, had focused on goals and deadlines, and would try looking into personal motivations. He thanked Arthur and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold felt hopeful and relieved. He believed Arthur’s advice could help.
- In a team meeting, Harold proposed quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each team member. He heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each person and wanted the project to succeed together.
- Later, Harold observed that the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- Harold told Arthur he tried the suggestions but the team still was not responding. Arthur said there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold agreed to set up another round of meetings. He became determined and focused, believing there might be underlying issues he had not addressed.
- In one-on-one meetings, Harold asked team members to share concerns or problems. He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few people that was affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold told Team Member 1 he would look into resolving conflicts. He told Team Member 2 he understood, would see if tasks could be redistributed, and that their well-being was important.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered. He believed addressing individual concerns would improve team performance and intended to create a more supportive, open team environment.
- In a team meeting, Harold announced regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help them work better together. He heard Team Member 2 agree and say it was good that their concerns were being addressed. Harold said he was glad, wanted everyone to work together for success, and that their input and well-being were crucial.
